correctness.rationale: The repaired RESULT.md states explicitly the conditional normal law already used in the frozen proof: knowledge of conditional mean and variance alone does not imply the mixture. For example, an equal conditional mixture of centered normals with variances dV(s) and 3dV(s) has the stated variance but a heavier far tail. The repair also fixes the Bayes version for every x≠0; densities and conditional versions at zero are not needed. Integration of the positive variance kernel gives as-ac plus the positive remainder H(2H-1) exp(-s/tau) times the integral of r(s+r)^(2H-2) exp(-r/tau) over r>0. Thus the rescaled phase is u+w+1/(uR_q), with R_q<=w and q times the difference from u+w+1/(uw) tending to lambda*c/(uw^2) uniformly on positive compacts. The latter comparison phase has a unique minimum 3 and Hessian [[2,1],[1,2]]. For localization, putting v=1/(uR_q) makes the singular amplitude factor R_q^(-1/2)=sqrt(u)sqrt(v). One unit of the exponent absorbs sqrt(v), leaving integrable gamma weights and the uniform phase gap off the saddle. The convergent local Gaussian integral has factor 2*pi/(q sqrt(3)); the Jacobian and likelihood give q^(alpha+k-1) sqrt(lambda)/(sqrt(4*pi*a*beta) Gamma(alpha) Gamma(k)). The finite intercept produces exp(-lambda*c), not an extra power of q. Normalization of the same localized density gives inverse Hessian covariance and limiting Gaussian correlation -1/2.
residual_risks: Finite quadrature is only a check, not a certificate. Weak convergence identifies the correlation of the limiting Gaussian; it need not by itself establish convergence of raw conditional Pearson correlations. The theorem is for fixed time and parameters, not simultaneous distance/time or tempering limits.
